page: Amazon Web Services r5.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor running at 3.1 GHz. The system provides 96 virtual CPUs across 48 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled. It is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, but it delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores, alongside high memory bandwidth, reaching 4503.04 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 220.3 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Redis SET operations perform exceptionally well at 74.62 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is strong at 46.46 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by lower scores in single-threaded stress-ng and gzip compression tests. LLM text generation speeds are also limited, particularly for medium-sized models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r5.24xlarge offers high memory density relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The high memory bandwidth and strong multi-core capabilities make this instance well-suited for large-scale in-memory databases like Redis, high-throughput web serving, distributed caching, and enterprise database operations.
